gaps.sentence: Parcels ___ (leave) in the porch if nobody is home.
gaps.explanation: Modal passive: should be + left. A recommendation; 'are left' (routine) is also acceptable.

gaps.sentence: The winners ___ (GIVE) their medals by the mayor last night.
gaps.explanation: 'Last night' + agent 'by the mayor': past simple passive were given.

gaps.sentence: They're getting the garden ___ (landscape) this spring.
gaps.explanation: Causative with get: are getting + the garden + landscaped.

gaps.sentence: She hates ___ (interrupt) when she's deep in work.
gaps.explanation: Passive gerund: being + past participle, after verbs like hate, like, avoid.

gaps.sentence: Several issues remain ___ (resolve) before the launch.
gaps.explanation: 'Remain' + passive infinitive (to be resolved) expresses unfinished business.

gaps.sentence: The stairs ___ (reinforce) when part of the ceiling gave way.
gaps.hint: action in progress at a past moment
gaps.explanation: Past continuous passive: was/were being + past participle, interrupted by a sudden past event.
The policy receives the action: 'will be introduced'.

gaps.sentence: There's still a lot of paperwork ___ (complete) before we can close the account.
gaps.explanation: Noun + passive to-infinitive (paperwork to be completed) — the paperwork receives the action.
